# 4 Ezra Chapter 11 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## 11:7 — eagle's speech to wings

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "voice-its-utterances to-its-feathers" | Literal — vocem mittere |
| LOGOS | "give voice to its feathers" | More natural English |
| PNEUMA | "spoke to its feathers" | Simplest |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** "Give voice to its feathers" (LOGOS). "Utterance" in EMET is slightly forced; LOGOS is clearest while preserving the formal register.

---

## 11:8 — the eagle's instruction to wings

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "Wake-not-all-at-once! Sleep-each-in-his-own-place, and-wake-in-order" | Literal |
| LOGOS | "Do not all wake at once! Let each sleep in his own place, and wake in order" | Same in natural English |
| PNEUMA | "Do not all wake at once. Each of you sleep in your place and rise in turn." | Rephrased |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** "Do not all wake at once! Let each sleep in his own place, and wake in order" (LOGOS). The exclamation mark after the first command is appropriate for the commanding tone.

---

## 11:35 — the lion from the forest (Messiah)

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "a-creature-like-a-lion was-roused-out-of-the-forest-roaring" | Literal |
| LOGOS | "a creature like a lion was roused out of the forest roaring" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "from the forest a creature like a lion came charging out with a roar" | More dynamic |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** "A creature like a lion was roused out of the forest roaring" (LOGOS). "Roused" captures the passive implication (it was summoned or stirred up) better than PNEUMA's "charging out."

---

## 11:40 — the eagle's injustice catalogue

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "you-have-afflicted-the-meek and-injured-the-peaceable and-hated-the-truthful and-loved-liars" | Full parallel literal |
| LOGOS | "you have afflicted the meek and injured the peaceable and hated the truthful and loved liars" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "You crushed the weak. You harmed the peaceful. You despised the honest and embraced the deceitful." | Split into four sentences |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** LOGOS — the whole catalogue as one accumulating sentence preserves the rhetorical weight of the lion's indictment.

---

## 11:43 — the doom catalogue

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "you-and-your-horrible-wings and-your-hateful-feathers and-your-evil-heads and-your-dreadful-claws and-your-whole-vain-body" | Full list with hyphens |
| LOGOS | "you and your terrible wings and your hateful feathers and your evil heads and your dreadful claws and your whole vain body" | Full list, no hyphens |
| PNEUMA | "you and your dreadful wings, your loathsome feathers, your wicked heads, your terrible claws, your entire worthless body" | Rephrased with different adjectives |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** LOGOS with PNEUMA's substitution of "hateful feathers" kept. "Terrible wings / hateful feathers / evil heads / dreadful claws / vain body" — LOGOS adjectives throughout except PNEUMA's "hateful" for pennas tuas odiosas is actually more precise.

---

## Total disagreements: 5
